main.job: identity: says what someone or something is (am/is/are)
main.why: The identity link; invariant for person, used in every introduction.
The first working verb frame; carries the person prefixes every other verb form reuses.
Want is a building-block job; nataka is used in every shop and café.

main.job: location and current state: niko, uko, yuko
main.why: How Swahili says where someone is; English speakers wrongly use ni for this.

main.job: existence: there is / there are (negative hakuna)
main.why: Existence and availability; asked daily in shops and homes.
Lets the learner tell what happened; core of A2 storytelling.
Possession; Swahili has no separate have verb, so it must be taught as a unit.

main.job: negation of present actions: negative prefix, no -na-, verb ends in -i
main.why: Negation is a building block; Swahili marks it on the verb, not with a separate 'not'.
Must is a building-block job; very frequent in daily plans.
Plans and promises; completes the core tense set.
Can is a building-block job and the everyday way to ask for help.

main.job: done and still true now (perfect); many states: nimechoka
main.why: Used constantly for states (tired, full, arrived); English speakers use -na- instead.

spares.why: Go is a building-block job; keeps ku- in tensed forms (ninakwenda).
Come is a building-block job; keeps ku- in tensed forms (ninakuja).

spares.job: marks a yes/no question at the start of a sentence
spares.why: Optional question marker heard in careful speech and writing.

jobs_covered.people reference: person prefixes ni-/u-/a-/tu-/m-/wa- taught inside -na- (pronouns are usually dropped)
jobs_covered.yes/no questions: rising intonation, no word needed (je is spare s03)
jobs_covered.wh-questions: question-word set (nini, nani, wapi, lini, gani, vipi, -ngapi) is too big for 12 slots; not started
jobs_covered.go/come: not covered at this count (spares s01, s02)

shape.notes: Bare A2 slice with no known items, so building blocks and the core tense set take every slot. No greetings (A2 filter). Go/come and wh-words are the next items in line.
